title: Three Years and One Short Lamp
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：pile　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pile 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the grandmother ① sorted the pile that no child in the courtyard would have described, and he said the sorting was the whole of the year. The ② pile, meaning the heap itself and not the lamp, ran three years and stayed undescribed in the book; a pile, he said, is the only thing in a courtyard that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ pile in that courtyard had the same short lamp beside it, and the ④ pile at the far window, meaning the gift they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A pile, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the grandmother said the describing is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the pile was the whole of the matter, meaning the load and not the heap. The ⑥ pile, meaning the load and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; pile, he said, is either something you sort or the only word that means both a heap and a load. He said the load is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ pile had become a line in a diary, and the diary had become an argument about the short lamp. The ⑧ pile of the whole thing, the grandmother wrote in February, was one courtyard and three years of describing; pile, he said, is either the gift at the far window or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ pile I remember is the heap described in the diary, which closed in 1973 and is still described as the quietest in the courtyard. A ⑩ pile, my mother said in 1975, is the only heap that improves by being described; every pile, she said, is a load that has agreed to look like a heap. She said the load was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 堆；一叠（指院子里每一堆旁边的那一堆）
B. n. 堆；一叠（指那堆堆本身，与小小的灯相对）
C. 固定搭配：sort the pile 理这一堆堆
D. n. 堆；一叠（指留给孩子们守着的那一件）
E. n. 堆之事（抽象总称，指一处院子的堆之事）
F. n. 堆；一叠（指日记里写到、被描述的那一堆）
G. n. 堆、重负（指一件事里人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 重负（抽象总称，指人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: sorted the pile that no child in the courtyard would have described
The pile, meaning the heap itself and not the lamp
the pile at the far window

answers.why: sort the pile 意为“理这一堆堆”，1966 年那位祖母把院子里没有一位孩子肯描述的一堆堆做了一遍。
pile 意为“堆；一叠”，指那堆堆本身而不是小小的灯，它经过了三个年头而在簿子上没有被描述。
pile 意为“堆；一叠”，指院子里每一堆旁边的那一堆，每一堆旁边都有同一盏小小的灯。
pile 意为“堆；一叠”，指最远那扇窗边的留给孩子们守着的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
pile 意为“堆、重负”，指一件事里人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这堆重负就是那件事的全部。
pile 意为“重负”，指人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西而不是那堆堆，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
pile 意为“堆；一叠”，指日记里写到、被描述的那一堆，到 1971 年这一堆成了日记里的一行。
pile 意为“堆之事”，祖母二月写道，整件事的堆之事是一处院子和三个年头的描述。
pile 意为“堆；一叠”，我记得的是日记里描述过的那一堆，1973 年过完了，至今仍被说成院子里最安静的一堆。
pile 为抽象总称，母亲 1975 年说，堆是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的堆。
